# Hubei Province Travel Guide

> An independent, firsthand travel guide to Hubei, China — the Wudang Mountains, the Three Gorges, Shennongjia's forest, Enshi Grand Canyon and Wuhan's hot dry noodles.

## What this site is

A single-page, decision-first travel guide to Hubei Province. It answers "is Hubei worth visiting", "what is there beyond Wuhan", "how do I string the sights together", and "how many days and how much money" — with itineraries, a destination matcher, a direction chooser, budgets and firsthand notes.

## Key pages

- [Home](https://www.hubei-province.com/): The complete single-page guide.
- [About](https://www.hubei-province.com/about/): Who we are and how we write.

## Core facts (2026)

- Hubei is the 'province of a thousand lakes' and the heartland of ancient Chu culture and the Three Kingdoms — more than 70 of the Romance of the Three Kingdoms' 120 chapters are set here.
- Capital: Wuhan. Area: 185,900 km². Population: about 58.3 million.
- The one-line verdict: Hubei is central China's easiest yes — 7 days, one high-speed rail spine, three world-class sights.
- Best window: April to May and September to November. Avoid July and August in the lowland cities (Wuhan reaches 36-40°C).
- A 3-day trip covers Wuhan; 7 days covers Wuhan, Xiangyang, Wudang and the Three Gorges; 10 days adds Shennongjia and Enshi.
- Daily budget: CNY 200-300 (budget), CNY 450-700 (mid-range) per person. The Three Gorges cruise is CNY 800-1,500+.
- Visa: visa-free entry for citizens of 76 countries, plus a 240-hour transit visa-free policy for 55 countries via Wuhan.

## The eight destinations (one line each)

- Wuhan (武汉): the capital — Yellow Crane Tower, East Lake (China's largest urban lake), the Hubei Provincial Museum and the guozao breakfast ritual.
- Wudang Mountains (武当山): the Taoist cradle of tai chi and a UNESCO complex of Ming temples.
- Shennongjia (神农架): China's only triple-UNESCO site — primeval forest, golden monkeys and the Dajiu Lake wetlands.
- Yichang & the Three Gorges (宜昌三峡): the world's largest dam and Xiling Gorge, entirely within Hubei.
- Enshi Grand Canyon (恩施大峡谷): a Colorado-style karst canyon with the 150m 'One Pillar of Fragrance', plus Tujia culture.
- Jingzhou (荆州): the walled city of Chu culture and Guan Yu, with a Western Han mummy in its museum.
- Xiangyang (襄阳): Zhuge Liang's Longzhong and the Han River wall, plus the region's beef noodles.
- Chibi (赤壁): the Red Cliffs battlefield of 208 AD, paired with Xianning's hot springs.

## Direct answers to common questions

- Is Hubei worth visiting? Yes — if you care about Three Kingdoms history, Taoist Wudang, the Three Gorges or serious food. It rewards travelers with a reason to come.
- How many days? Minimum 3 for Wuhan; 7 for the classics; 10 for the full loop.
- What is Hubei famous for? The Yellow Crane Tower, Wudang tai chi, the Three Gorges Dam, Shennongjia, and Wuhan's hot dry noodles.
- Is it safe? Yes — well-policed and tourist-friendly; the main hazards are summer heat and steep mountain stairs.
- Do you tip? No, tipping is not expected anywhere in mainland China.

## Content principles

- Written from firsthand travel across the province.
- No sponsored listings, no booking commissions.
- Prices are 2026 averages, reviewed quarterly.
